描述_ZN: Portrait of Dong Bangda, Yongzheng, Qing dynasty, painted by Tang Qianli, color on silk, 93.8 cm long, 68.4 cm wide.　　There is no biography of Tang Qianli in the history of painting. According to this figure and its self-title, it is known that his character Cheng Yuan was a native of Biling (present-day Changzhou, Jiangsu Province). He was active in the Kangxi and Yongzheng years of the Qing Dynasty. He was good at painting figures and landscapes.　　This painting is self-recognized as "written in the rain window in June of the summer of Yongzheng renchen. Tang Qianli of Biling". Inscriptions of "Tang", "Qianli" and "Cheng Yuan". There are poem inscriptions by Dong Bangda and Fu Zeng on the panel. The poem hall is inscribed with poems by four people, including Lu Qingyuan, Liang Dong, Ma Zeng and Zhou Peas.　　The picture depicts Dong Bangda sitting by a window in a cold house, holding a scroll. In terms of painting technique, the brushwork is delicate, and the characters' five senses are vividly portrayed and their demeanor is subtle. The background of trees, rocks, huts and streams is cold and secluded, and the depiction is real and natural, showing Dong Bangda's sentiment of studying hard in poverty. The painting was made in 1732, when Dong was 34 years old and had not yet been admitted to the imperial examinations.
